label: DefiCohomologia
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{DefiCohomologia} Let $k$ be a field.  An \textit{oriented cohomology theory} is a contravariant functor $A\,$ from the category of smooth quasi-projective varieties over $k\,$ into the category of commutative rings. Part of the data are also \textit{direct images for projective morphisms}; that is to say,  a morphism of groups $f_*\colon A(Y)\to A(X)$, for any projective morphism $f\colon Y\to X$, such that
$\mathrm{Id}_*=\mathrm{Id}$, $(fg)_*=f_*g_*\,$ and such that the projection formula
$f_*(f^*(x)y)=xf_*(y)$ holds.

On an oriented cohomology theory $\,A$, any smooth closed subvariety $\,i\colon Z\to X\,$ has a \textit{fundamental class}
$$\,[Z]^A\coloneqq i_*(1)\in A(X)\ ,$$ and any line
bundle $\,L\to X\,$ has a \textit{Chern class} $$\,c_1^A(L)\coloneqq s_0^*(s_{0*}(1))\in A(X) \ , $$ where $\,s_0\colon X\to L\,$ is the zero section.


These data are also assumed to satisfy the following axioms:
\begin{enumerate}
\item
The ring morphism $i_1^*+i_2^*\colon A(X_1\amalg X_2)\to A(X_1)\oplus A(X_2)$ is an
isomorphism, where $i_j\colon X_j\to X_1\amalg X_2$ is the natural immersion (in particular, $A(\emptyset )=0$).

\item For any affine bundle
$\pi \colon P\to X$,                                                  
the ring morphism $\pi ^*\colon A(X)\to A(P)$ is an isomorphism.


\item
For any smooth closed subvariety $i\colon Z \to X$,  the following is an exact sequence: $$\
A(Z)\xrightarrow{i_*}A(X)\xrightarrow{j^*}A(X-Z)\ .$$

\item
If a morphism $f\colon \bar X\to X$ is transversal to a smooth closed subvariety
$i\colon Z\to X$ of codimension $d$,                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   
then the following square is commutative:
$$
\xymatrix{A(Z) \ar[r]^-{f^*} \ar[d]^{i _*} & A(\bar Z) \ar[d]^{i _*}\\ A(X)
\ar[r]^-{f^*} & A(\bar X). }
$$

\item
For any morphism $f\colon
Y\to X$ and any projective bundle $\pi \colon \mathbb{P}(E)\to X$,  the following square is commutative:
$$
\xymatrix{A(\mathbb{P}(E))\ar[r]^-{f^*} \ar[d]^{\pi _*} & A(\mathbb{P}(f^*E))
\ar[d]^{\pi _*}\\ A(X) \ar[r]^-{f^*} & A(Y). }
$$

\item If $E\to X$ is a vector bundle of rank $r+1$, then the $A(X)$-module in $A(\mathbb{P}(E))$ is free of rank $r+1$:
$$
A(\mathbb{P}(E))=A(X)\oplus A(X)x_E\oplus \ldots \oplus A(X)x_E^r.
$$ where $x_E=c_1^A(\xi
_E)$ is the first Chern class of the tautological
line bundle.
\end{enumerate}


                                                                                                                                                        

A \textit{morphism of cohomologies} $\varphi \colon A\to \bar A\,$ is a natural transformation preserving direct images; 
i.e.,  it is a morphism of functors of rings $\,\varphi \colon A\to \bar A\,$ such that
$$
\varphi (f_*(a))=\bar f_*(\varphi (a))
$$
for any projective morphism $f\colon Y\to X$ and any element $a\in A(Y)$.
head: environment

title: Example
body_md:
\begin{enumerate}
\item
Weil cohomologies are oriented cohomologies in the sense above. These examples include singular cohomology of complex varieties, de Rham cohomology of varieties over a field $k$ of characteristic zero, or $l$-adic cohomology, with $k$ of characteristic different from $l\,$.

\item
The Chow ring $\, CH^\bullet (X)\,$ of rational equivalence classes of algebraic cycles is also an oriented cohomology theory (\cite{Fulton}).

\item
Grothendieck's $K$-theory is an oriented cohomology theory where the cohomology rings $\,K(X)\,$ have no graduation (v. gr., \cite{ExpositionesI}).


                                    
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       



\item
Algebraic cobordism $\, \Omega^{\bullet} (X)$, as constructed by Levine and Morel (\cite{LevineMorel}), is also an oriented cohomology.
\end{enumerate}

label: Jouanolou
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{Jouanolou}
For any quasi-projective $k$-variety $\,X$, there exists an affine bundle $\,P \to X\,$ such that $\,P\,$ is an affine variety.

label: LeyGrupoFormal
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{LeyGrupoFormal}
Let $\,A\,$ be an oriented cohomology theory.  There exists a unique commutative formal group law $\,f^A(u,v)\in \,A(*)[[u,v]]\,$ such that
$$ c_1^A (L_x \otimes L_y) = f^A(x,y) $$ for any pair of line bundles $L_x$, $L_y$, with Chern classes $x := c_1^A (L_x)$ and $y := c_1^A (L_y)$.

We say that $A$ {\it follows the law} $f^A$, or that the series $f^A(u,v)$ is the {\it formal group law associated to $A$}.

title: Definition
body_md:
The {\it Chern classes} $c_n^A(E)\in A(X)$ of a vector bundle $E\to X$ of rank $r$ are the coefficients of the characteristic polynomial
$c(E)=x^r-c_1^A(E)x^{r-1}+\ldots +(-1)^rc_r^A(E)$ of the endomorphism of the free
$A(X)$-module $A(\mathbb{P}(E))$ defined by the multiplication by $x_E=c_1^A(\xi
_E)$, so that
$$
x_E^r-c_1^A(E)x_E^{r-1}+\ldots +(-1)^rc_r^A(E)=0 \ . 
$$

label: ExtensionesDeSeries
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{ExtensionesDeSeries}
Let $A$ be an oriented cohomology and $\,F \in A(*)[[t]]\,$ be any series.

\begin{itemize}
\item {\bf Multiplicative extension}: There exists a unique morphism of functor of monoids,                                                       
$$ 
F_\times \colon K^+ \longrightarrow (A , \cdot )  \ , 
$$ 
whose value on the the tautological line bundles is  $ F_\times (\xi_d) := F(x_d)$.

\item {\bf Additive extension}: There exists a unique morphism of functor of groups                                                 
$$ F_+ \colon K \longrightarrow A   \ , $$ whose value on the tautological line bundles  is $\, F_+ (\xi_d)  := F(x_d)$.
\end{itemize}

label: SerieInversa
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{SerieInversa} If the series $\,F\,$ is invertible, then $\,F_\times\,$ extends to a natural transformation of groups $\, F_\times \colon K \longrightarrow (A^* , \cdot )$ that takes values in the multiplicative group $A^*$ of units of the cohomology.
Moreover, for any element $a \in K(X)$,
$$ F_\times (-a) = F_\times (a)^{-1} = (F^{-1})_\times (a) \ . $$

label: EjMorfismos
title: Example
body_md:
\label{EjMorfismos}
\begin{enumerate}
\item
Any morphism of functor of rings $\,\varphi \colon K \to K\,$ is  the additive extension, $\varphi = F_+$, of a unique series $\, F \in \mathbb{Z} [[t]]\,$ satisfying
\begin{equation*}
F( x + y - xy ) = F(x) \cdot F(y) \ .
\end{equation*}For any integer $\,j$, the series $\, (1-t)^{j} $ satisfies this condition.

The {\it Adams operation} $\,\psi^j \colon K \to K\,$ is the additive extension of the series\footnote{The minus sign in the exponent is chosen in order to agree with the classical definition.} $\,(1-t)^{-j}$. These operations are morphisms of rings $\,\psi^j \colon K(X)  \longrightarrow K (X)\,$ that, for a non-zero $j$, act on line bundles as follows:
$$ \psi^j (L_x) = (1-x)^{-j} = \left( 1 - \left( 1 - L_x^{-1} \right) \right)^{-j}  = L_x^{j} \ , $$ where 
$\,x = c_1^K (L_x) = 1 - L_x^{-1}$. In particular,  $\,\psi^{-1}(L)=L^*$.

                                                                                                  
                

\item 
If $A$ follows the additive law and $A(*)$ is a $\mathbb{Q}$-algebra,  the exponential series $$\exp (t) := \sum_n \frac{t^n}{n!}\,  \in A(*) [[t]] $$
fulfills equation (\ref{MorfismoFGL}), and therefore its additive extension $\mathrm {ch} \colon K \to A$ is a morphism of rings, called the {\it Chern character}.

\item 
Let $A(*)$ be a ring where $1, 2, \ldots , p-1$ are units, and that contains a nilpotent element $\varepsilon$ such that $\varepsilon^p = 0$ (for example, $k [\varepsilon]/ (\varepsilon^p)$ with $k$ a field with characteristic zero or bigger or equal than $p$). If, moreover, $A$ follows the additive law, then the twisted exponential
$$ \exp_{\varepsilon} (t) := \exp ( \varepsilon \, t) = 1 + \varepsilon \, t + \ldots + \frac{\varepsilon^{p-1}}{(p-1)!}\, t^{p-1} \in A(*) [t] $$
also satisfies equation (\ref{MorfismoFGL}), and hence its additive extension $\mathrm {ch}_{\varepsilon} \colon K \to A$ is a morphism of rings, that we call {\it twisted Chern character}.

\end{enumerate}

label: EjemSeries
title: Example
body_md:
\label{EjemSeries}
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $A$ follows the additive law, then the series associated to $ s_m \colon K \to \bar{A}$ is the monomial $(-t)^{m-1}$:
$$ s_m (x_d) \, = \, s_m (1 - \xi^*_d) \, = \, 0 - \bar{y}_d^m \, = \,- (-\bar{x}_d)^m \, = \, (-\bar{x}_d)^{m-1} \bar{x}_d \ . $$


\item  The series associated to the Adams operation $\psi^j \colon K \to K $ is the polynomial
$$ \mathsf{B}^j := \frac{1 - (1-t)^{j}}{t}\ = \ j - \binom{j}{2} t +  \ldots + (-1)^{j-1}t^{j-1} \ ,$$
because
$$\psi^j (x_d )  \, =\, \psi^j (1 - \xi_d^* ) \, =\, 1 - (\xi_d^*)^j = 1 - (1-x_d)^{j} \, = \, \left( \frac{1 - (1-x_d)^{j}}{x_d} \right) x_d  \ .
$$



\item If $A$ follows the additive  law and $A(*)$ is a $\mathbb{Q}$-algebra,  then
the series associated to the Chern character $\mathrm {ch} \colon K \to A$ is $ \frac{1-e^{-t}}{t}$:
$$
\mathrm {ch} (x_d )  \, =\, \mathrm {ch} (1 - \xi_d^* ) \, =\, 1 - e^{y_d} \, = \, 1 - e^{-x_d} \, = \, \left( \frac{1-e^{-x_d}}{x_d} \right)\, x_d \ ,
$$
(observe it is the inverse of the standard {\it Todd series} $ \operatorname{Td} (t) :=  \frac{t}{1-e^{-t}}$).

\item If $A$ follows the additive law and $A(*)$ is as in Example \ref{EjMorfismos}.3, then the series associated to the twisted Chern character $\mathrm {ch}_{\varepsilon} \colon K \to A$ is 
$$
\frac{1-\exp_\varepsilon (- t)}{t}= \varepsilon- \frac{\varepsilon^2}{2}\,t + \ldots + \frac{\varepsilon^{p-1}}{(p-1)!}\, (-t)^{p-2}  .
$$


        
               
                                                                                                                                                                                         
                                                                                                                                         
             


                                                                                                                      
     
                                         
                                                                       
                 


         
             
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  
                                         
                                                                       
                 
           
                                                                                                                                                                         
                                                                                                                                                                                 
                                                                                                                                                       
                                                         
             
                                                      
                                                                                                               
     

\end{enumerate}

title: Definition
body_md:
Let $\bar{A}$ be an oriented cohomology theory and let $\,\mathrm{S} \in \bar{A}(*)[[t]]^*\,$ be an invertible series. The {\it modified direct image} $\,f_*^{\mathrm{S}}\,$ of a projective morphism $f \colon Y \to X$ is defined as
$$f^{\mathrm{S}}_{* } \, := \, \mathrm{S}_{\times} (T_X) f_* \left( \mathrm{S}_{\times} \left( T_Y \right)^{-1} \cdot \ \underline{\phantom{a}}\  \right)\, =\, f_* \left( \mathrm{S}_{{\times}} (-T_f) \cdot \ \underline{\phantom{a}}\  \right)   \ ,$$ 
where $T_f := T_Y - f^* T_X \in K(Y)$ is the virtual relative tangent bundle. That is to say, $\, f^\mathrm{S}\,$ is the dotted arrow that makes this square commutative:
$$
\xymatrix{
\bar{A}(Y) \ar[d]_{\mathrm{S}_\times (T_Y)^{-1}\, \cdot  }  \ar@{..>}[rr]^-{f_*^{\mathrm{S}} }  & & \bar{A}(X)  \\
\bar{A}(Y)  \ar[rr]^-{f_*}   & & \bar{A}(X) \ar[u]_{\cdot \, \mathrm{S}_\times (T_X) } \ . }
$$
head: environment

label: Modificacion
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{Modificacion} The functor $\bar{A}$ endowed with  the modified direct images $f^\mathrm{S}_*$ is an oriented cohomology theory, that we denote $(\bar{A} , f_{*}^{\mathrm{S}})$.  Moreover, if we write $\bar{x}^{\mathrm{S}}_d$ for the Chern class of $\xi_d$ in $(\bar{A} , f_{*}^{\mathrm{S}})$, then
$$
\bar{x}^{\mathrm{S}}_d \, = \, \mathrm{S}(\bar{x}_d)\,\bar{x}_d \ . 
$$

label: RR
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{RR} 
Let $\,\varphi \colon A\to \bar{A}\,$ be a morphism of functor of rings whose associated series $\mathrm{S} \in \bar{A}(*)[[t]] $ is invertible. Then $\varphi$ is a morphism of cohomologies
$$ \varphi \colon \ A \ \longrightarrow \left( \bar{A} \, , \, f_{*}^{\mathrm{S}} \right) \ .$$

In other words, for any projective morphism $\,f \colon Y \to X\,$ between smooth quasi-projective $k$-varieties, the diagram below commutes
$$
\xymatrix{
A(Y)  \ar[rrr]^-{f_*} \ar[d]_{\varphi} & & & A(X) \ar[d]^{\varphi} \\
\bar{A}(Y) \ar[rrr]^-{f_* \left( \mathrm{S}_{\times} (-T_f) \cdot \ \underline{\phantom{a}}\  \right) } & & & \bar{A} (X)}  \ .
$$
